simple.meaning: טוֹפָפָה (ṭôwphâphâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a fillet for the forehead.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, beginning at Exodus 13:16. Its contexts include Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טוֹפָפָה (H2903).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: טוֹפָפָה (ṭôwphâphâh) / H2903 is traced through Exodus 13:16, Deuteronomy 6:8, Deuteronomy 11:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H2903. totaphoth טוֺטָפוֺת noun feminine plural bands (Late Hebrew טוֺטֶפֶת Aramaic טוֺטֶפְתָּא and especially plural טוטפין id. ) — always bands, frontlet-bands, between the eyes (|| יד על אוֺת ; compare עֵינֶיךָ בֵּין זִכָּרוֺן Exod 13:9 || id. ); figurative of dedication of firstborn עיניך בין לְטוֺטָפֹת ֗֗֗ וְהָיָה 13:16 (JE); of commandments of לְטו ׳וְהָיוּ ׳י, Deut 11:18 and לְטֹטָפת וְהָיוּ 6:8 . — This injunction, originally figurative for perpetual remembrance (otherwise Kn, and Klein l.c. 666 ff. , see above, Benz Archaeology 111 Now Archaeology i. 134 ), was taken literally by later Jews, and hence the custom of wearing phylacteries ; see Di (on Exod 13:16 ) Winer RE Ri HWB (article Denkzettel ) Smith Dict.
